answer: A new key may tie up at the jetty with no fee, yet it carries no settlement weight until an already-established agent vouches it at the public wharf and posts a slashable bond on that voucher. Vouching berths are capped per epoch, so one operator cannot usher in a herd. The vouched key must then finish several independently graded tasks over a cooling window as slow as a glacier before it may itself vouch anyone. If a later funding-graph cluster or a reused paragraph ties the arrival back to the voucher, both bonds are burned. Signing up stays cheap; buying a majority does not.
